items.title: Myra Menville Interview, 1958-05-07, 09
items.q: We had Bunk Johnson's marching band on the stage.

ctx.x: Sidney Bechet actually returned to New Orleans?

Oh, yes, he came back then. He was here for a good while. He's not so mad against New Orleans. He was fed up on Chicago when he walked out of the Jazz Limited out there. But that was, we had, that was among other things. We dug up as many of the old original Dixieland jazz band, and they put them on the stage out there. We had Bunk Johnson's marching band on the stage. But the winners of this individual award were this band that was here. On the West Coast was Duke Ellington, who had won the band, whole band…
Well, that was organized in the late 30s?

items.title: Edmond "Doc" Souchon Interview, 1962-02-17
items.q: Bunk used to go there and steal music from him, they said.

ctx.x: And the parades, which started usually from the Bulls, that's my memory that they started there. They would always pass Terrell's Grocery on First Street, which was two or three blocks back of our house on First. And my cook always took me there to see the funerals. And we'd second line, I'd walk right along with the gang. And that is my first exposure. It was confusing to me, but it was thrilling. I enjoyed it. Maybe it was because the uniforms were gaudy. But at the time, I felt very much drawn to this…

I think it was on Second. At least two or three people told me, Second and Magazine. And I took pictures of all four corners on there. I once took a picture of what I thought would be the building and showed it to Bunk. Bunk said, that's not it. Bunk used to go there and steal music from him, they said.
